ua: Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 18_7 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/27.2 Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1
measurement: BrowserStack Automate real-device iPhone Safari sessions (2026-11-17), no proxy and no Local tunnel: each request is sent by the device's own network stack straight to https://tls.peet.ws/api/all, which answers with the HTTP/2 HEADERS frame it received (pseudo-headers and regular headers in received order, values verbatim); 'fields' is that frame's regular headers. Driver: WebDriver Navigate To (nav-typed; BrowserStack's start page https://appium.io/ is its referrer), a WebDriver Element Click on a same-origin link (nav-click), location.assign (nav-script), a link clicked on https://example.com/ (nav-cross-click), then same-origin page requests from the echo document: fetch GET, fetch GET with X-Alpha/X-Beta, XHR POST of a string body (XHR's own text/plain content-type, modelled as the page's first call), XHR POST with Content-Type, XHR POST with Content-Type/X-Probe-A/X-Probe-B, fetch POST with six page headers. Every session's TLS and HTTP/2 identity is the same (ja4 t13d2013h2_a09f3c656075_7f0f34a4126d, akamai 2:0;3:100;4:2097152;9:1|10420225|0|m,s,a,p).
recording_transport: Not available for https on these devices: routed through compat-http (BrowserStackLocal --force-local --force-proxy into an INTERCEPT session), Safari 27.2 shows 'This Connection Is Not Private' for the interception CA and its 'visit this website' control (WebDriver click, native XCUITest tap, the warning page's own visitInsecureWebsite / visitInsecureWebsiteWithTemporaryBypass commands) opens no bypass, and acceptInsecureCerts/acceptSsl do not pass it: the supervised BrowserStack iPhones refuse an untrusted certificate. compat-http did record the same session's plain http:// requests (ses_e53ab32cd47c25004d0b191077ce0341, BrowserStack 402443e9da0ec300826b8567e964762dcaeb90cb), but over http Safari sends no sec-fetch-* and adds upgrade-insecure-requests to every navigation, so those dictionaries are not the https ones and are not witnesses here.
equality: Every class's header order and every value but the per-session ones (user-agent, referer, accept-language, :path) are identical across Safari 27.2 (2 sessions, iPhone 18 Pro), 27.0 (iPhone 15, 15 Pro, 16 Pro Max, 18 Pro Max) and the 26.6.1 control (iPhone 17 Pro): Safari 27.x is the late generation byte for byte on these classes. No BrowserStack device runs 27.1 or 27.3.
falsification: A Safari 27.x capture of one of these classes whose order differs from the session's here, or whose Accept-Encoding is not 'gzip, deflate, br, zstd'.
